issues.legal_issue: A sale of service-grant land is invalid when binding local orders specifically prohibit its alienation.
material_facts: The disputed land formed part of a Patel service inam.
The land was sold to a person who was not the registered holder of the inam.
Applicable orders issued under the authority of the ruler specifically prohibited alienation of the service inam land.
The parties disputed title to the land on the basis of the sale.
issues.conclusion: The sale was invalid because the binding local orders prohibited alienation of the service inam land; the Bombay Hereditary Offices Act did not override those orders.
issues.legal_principle: The court construed the relevant Kolhapur Wat Hukums as having legal and binding force, and held that their specific prohibition on alienation governed despite the Bombay Hereditary Offices Act, 1874, as applied to Kolhapur. It relied on Rangappa Venappa Akole v. Laxman Malyappa, 62 Bom. L.R. 639, including its recognition that the Act did not override specific Wat Hukums.

predicates.service_grant_title_dispute: The parties disputed title to land granted as a service inam.
predicates.sale_of_service_grant_land: A holder sold land that formed part of a service grant.
predicates.binding_local_orders_prohibited_alienati: Orders issued under the ruler's authority prohibited alienation of the service-grant land.

issues.definition: When a title dispute concerns a sale of service-grant land prohibited by binding local orders, the transfer is invalid.

issues.legal_issue: The limitation rule requiring proof of dispossession by the defendant does not bar a title-based possession suit when the defendant did not dispossess the claimant.
material_facts: The suit sought ejectment and recovery of possession on the basis of title.
In relation to part of the land, the claimant's mother had possession after a mortgage was redeemed.
The government later took possession of that land and, when the attachment was vacated, delivered possession to the defendant rather than the claimant.
The court found that the defendant had not dispossessed the claimant.
issues.conclusion: The suit was not barred by limitation under Article 142 of the Limitation Act because the defendant had not dispossessed the claimant and the suit was against a person not entitled to possession.
issues.legal_principle: Article 142 of the Limitation Act did not apply because the suit was against a person not entitled to possession, and the defendant had not dispossessed the claimant. The court treated the claimant's right to sue for possession as arising when possession was delivered to the defendant instead of the claimant.

predicates.title_based_possession_suit: The claimant brought a suit to recover possession on the basis of title.
predicates.defendant_did_not_dispossess_claimant: The defendant did not remove the claimant from possession.

issues.definition: When a claimant brings a title-based possession suit and the defendant did not dispossess the claimant, the suit is not barred by limitation on that basis.
